steps.title: Index manuals and SOPs, chunked by machine and fault code
steps.what: Split 3 service manuals and the SOP book into 7 chunks, each tagged with machine and fault code (TF-IDF stand-in for embeddings + a vector store).
steps.code:
for sec in re.split(r"\n(?=## )", manual_md):
    mid, code = parse_heading(sec)
    idx.add(f"{mid}/{code}", sec, machine=mid, fault_code=code, kind="manual")
idx.build()

steps.title: Build an MCP server for the CMMS: read history, create orders
steps.what: cmms_mcp_server.py exposes two tools over MCP, backed by SQLite seeded with 23 work orders; an MCP client listed the tools and called one.

steps.title: The technician describes the fault; pull docs and past fixes
steps.what: From the chat message and the live alarm, the copilot pulled the F-200/E14 manual section, 2 SOPs, 7 past work orders and the latest sensor readings.
steps.code:
manual = idx.search(f"{machine} {fault} {msg}", k=1, machine=machine, kind="manual")
sops = idx.search("lockout ... " + msg, k=2, kind="sop")
history = cmms.get_work_order_history(machine, fault)   # MCP tool
sensors = latest reading per tag for (machine, line)

steps.title: Replay past incidents against technician-confirmed causes
steps.what: Re-ran 8 held-out incidents: the confirmed cause came first 3/8 times in manual order, 6/8 for the copilot before the write-back, 8/8 after.
steps.code:
rank = position of the confirmed cause in each ordering
mttr = search_min + rank * 20 min per cause checked + repair_min
first_time_fix = rank == 1

arch.label: Manuals + SOPs
arch.note: chunked by machine and fault code

story.situation: A bottling plant with two lines. When a filler or capper stops, a technician digs through PDFs and old work orders while the line loses about 300 bottles a minute.
story.constraints: The CMMS is the system of record, so the copilot reads and writes it through a narrow MCP server (two tools, plant service account). Answers must cite the manual section or work order they come from. Lockout and sanitation SOPs always come first.
story.replay: Reuse: docs-by-RAG plus system-of-record-by-MCP fits any field-service or IT-ops desk. Next time: get technicians to log the confirmed root cause in one tap, because that write-back is what makes the next answer better.
story.problem_cost: Mean time to repair of about 1.5 hours on E14 faults, much of it searching and trying causes in manual order.

metrics.first_time_fixes: 3/8 in manual order -> 8/8 with the copilot
metrics.repeat_failures: 3 of 23 past work orders were repeats within 14 days; wrong first fix (repeat risk) 5/8 -> 0/8
metrics.write_back_effect: top-1 6/8 before logging the O-ring fix -> 8/8 after
